intro: Four outbound campaigns into the US: Indian software and API companies winning direct conversations, and agencies and recruiters reaching US decision-makers. Every number below comes from a real campaign.

audiences.title: Indian firms selling to US companies
audiences.body: Software development, IT services and API manufacturers that rely on referrals, marketplaces or trade shows and want direct conversations with US buyers.

audiences.title: Agencies and recruiters with US clients
audiences.body: Agencies and specialist recruitment firms that need a steady flow of meetings with US marketing, engineering and talent leaders.

playsTitle: What worked in the United States

plays.title: Direct conversations instead of project marketplaces
plays.body: An Indian software firm reached CTOs, engineering heads and operations leaders at mid-sized US retail and logistics companies. Each message introduced one relevant capability and asked for a short discovery call.

plays.title: Open with the second-source question
plays.body: An Indian API manufacturer had a broad list but couldn't tell who needed a supplier now. Outreach to US procurement and sourcing leaders asked one direct question about second-source evaluation.

plays.title: Target employers with live vacancies
plays.body: A data engineering recruiter contacted talent leaders and engineering managers at US companies already advertising relevant roles, then qualified on urgency and agency process.

rulesBody: US B2B cold email falls under the CAN-SPAM Act, which doesn't require prior consent. It does require honest sender and subject lines, a physical postal address in every email and a working opt-out honoured within 10 business days.
timingBody: US time zones are 9.5 to 13.5 hours behind India. Messages are scheduled for the recipient's morning in their own time zone, and meetings land in US hours, which usually means evening calls for an India-based team.
